prompt.context: Your client is SPG, an international hotel chain that specializes in boutique luxury vacations. The client has over 500 properties worldwide, mostly concentrated in North America and Europe. These markets are highly correlated with the global economy. In an effort to diversify, SPG is focusing on Latin America. SPG is interested in opening another 200-room hotel in Costa Rica and has requested your consulting firm's help. There are several locations within Costa Rica suitable for the new location, and costs are relatively uniform throughout the country.
prompt.question:
1. What should SPG consider when evaluating site locations?
2. Since costs will be the same regardless of the site, which location offers the highest average daily revenue per room?

clarifying_info.a: The client has selected this market due to familiarity with the country and ease of doing business. They are not interested in alternatives.

clarifying_info.q: Does SPG already have hotels in Costa Rica?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, one other property located in Manual Antonio.

clarifying_info.q: What defines a boutique luxury hotel?
clarifying_info.a: All of SPG's hotels have 200 rooms and cater to the wealthy. As a result, rooms typically go for 50% more than the average rate, and total spend per room is 100% more than the average room.

exhibits.title: Map of Potential Locations
exhibits.shows: A map of Costa Rica showing four numbered candidate locations along with a data table of average room rates, average daily spend per room, existing SPG properties, and occupancy rates by symbol. A separate table shows the impact of hotel category (Budget vs. Luxury) on average rates and spend. Property information notes are also provided.

occupancy_legend.manual_antonio_note: Presence of another SPG property decreases occupancy by 50%

property_info.cannibalization_rule: Presence of another SPG property in the same location will decrease occupancy by 50%

framework: Entry Mode: Buy vs. Build vs. Partner — evaluate feasibility and timeline for each
Revenue Drivers: Room revenue (rate x occupancy), Food & Beverage, Activities/Amenities, ancillary spend
Market & Demand: Tourism trends in Costa Rica, seasonality, target customer segments
Competitive Landscape: Existing luxury hotels, competitive positioning
Risks: Economic/tourism volatility, cannibalization of existing SPG property, regulatory/political environment
Focus should be prioritized on Revenue given that costs are uniform across sites

questions.prompt: Which of the four candidate locations offers the highest average daily revenue per room? Walk through your calculation.
questions.guidance: A strong candidate states a hypothesis before calculating (e.g., 'I expect a beach or volcano destination to win on rate, but occupancy and cannibalization will matter'). The candidate applies the Luxury bonus to both room rate and daily spend, applies the occupancy rate, and flags the 50% cannibalization penalty at Manual Antonio. The answer is Arenal Volcano (Location 1) at $356.25 average daily spend per room. The candidate should then annualize: $356.25 x 360 days x 200 rooms = ~$25.65M annual revenue opportunity.

math.setup: For each location: Effective Room Rate = Base Rate x 1.5 (Luxury +50%). Effective Daily Spend = Base Spend x 2.0 (Luxury +100%). Total Spend per Room = Effective Room Rate + Effective Daily Spend. Revenue per Room per Day = Total Spend x Effective Occupancy. Manual Antonio occupancy is halved due to existing SPG property.
steps: Location 1 – Arenal Volcano: Room = $250 x 1.5 = $375. Spend = $50 x 2 = $100. Total = $475. Occupancy = 75%. Daily rev/room = $475 x 0.75 = $356.25
Location 2 – Guanacaste: Room = $300 x 1.5 = $450. Spend = $100 x 2 = $200. Total = $650. Occupancy = 50%. Daily rev/room = $650 x 0.50 = $325.00
Location 3 – San Jose: Room = $100 x 1.5 = $150. Spend = $25 x 2 = $50. Total = $200. Occupancy = 100%. Daily rev/room = $200 x 1.00 = $200.00
Location 4 – Manual Antonio: Room = $350 x 1.5 = $525. Spend = $150 x 2 = $300. Total = $825. Occupancy = 80% x 50% cannibalization = 40%. Daily rev/room = $825 x 0.40 = $330.00
Winner: Location 1 Arenal Volcano at $356.25 per room per day
Annualized: $356.25 x 360 days x 200 rooms = $25,650,000 per year
math.answer: Arenal Volcano (Location 1) at $356.25 average daily revenue per room; ~$25.65M annual revenue opportunity

brainstorming.prompt: Beyond room revenue, what are other sources of revenue a hotel should consider?

categories.name: Activities & Experiences
ideas: Fitness center memberships or day passes

recommendation: SPG should open the new 200-room hotel at Arenal Volcano (Location 1), which generates the highest average daily revenue per room at $356.25, yielding approximately $25.65M in annual revenue
The site avoids cannibalization risk (no existing SPG property) and benefits from strong occupancy at 75%
risks: Tourism volatility: Costa Rica market is still developing and could be affected by regional economic downturns or safety concerns
Competitive entry: Other luxury chains may also target Arenal Volcano, compressing rates over time
Seasonality: Occupancy assumptions may mask significant low-season dips; 75% average should be stress-tested
Construction/operational: Building in a volcano region may entail environmental regulations or higher unforeseen costs
Currency and political risk: Operating in an emerging market introduces FX and regulatory exposure
next_steps: Conduct detailed demand forecasting including seasonality analysis for Arenal Volcano
Perform site due diligence (land availability, zoning, environmental permits)
Benchmark competitive set at Arenal to validate the $250 base room rate assumption
Model full P&L including construction capex and operating costs to confirm positive NPV
Develop a phased opening plan leveraging learnings from the existing Manual Antonio property
